entries.message: This update includes add the Modern style, fold watched runs into stacks, and show one Up Next card per show, sync playlists with Plex, Emby, and Jellyfin, add automatic playlists, and fix large backups and restores, and faster seasons and sign-in checks, Jellyfin episode fallback, backup log and dashboard fixes.
entries.author: Lasikiewicz
details: Added a Classic/Modern switch in the sidebar, just above the Light/Dark toggle; the choice is remembered in this browser and works with both light and dark mode

The Modern style restyles the dashboard in dark and light mode: rounded gradient cards that lift on hover, provider-coloured Plex, Emby, and Jellyfin names, quieter field labels, and a highlighted active sidebar item
In the Modern style, dashboard cards show the title's backdrop artwork behind their details, and the dashboard background shows the artwork of the item at the top, shaded so text stays readable

In the Modern style, the featured Up Next card stretches across the top panel while nothing is playing, with its Clear button and progress bar; the heading reads Up Next while idle and Now Playing during playback
In the Modern style, playing sessions use the same backdrop layout side by side, with their details stacked one per line
The Now Playing section blurs the dashboard background like the sections below it, and the yellow hover border no longer fades at rounded corners
On phones, the Modern Up Next feature is a compact card with the poster beside the details

In the Modern style, episodes of the same show watched in a row fold into one run card showing the episode range and count, drawn as a stack with the older episodes' posters peeking out to the right; hovering spreads the stack a little

A button beside the TV Shows and Movies Recently watched titles folds that row's cards into their posters; clicking a folded poster or stack opens it, and opening another card folds the open one closed again. The choice is remembered per row
History cards mode takes the Modern card look in dark and light, with folded runs like the dashboard TV row
History grid posters and list mode get rounded corners, accent hovers, a tinted list header and readable provider badges in the Modern style
Under the Modern style, Discover, Watchlist, Ratings and custom list cards take the dashboard card look, with the rating as a small pill
Movies and TV cards and overview cards show the rounded Modern card surface and accent hover, and their provider labels are readable in light and dark mode
Movie and show pages in the Modern style get rounded posters, a card-style season list, episode tiles with an accent hover, and tidier fact labels
Settings sections and their expandable rows get rounded corners, a soft gradient surface and an accent hover border in the Modern style
Up Next shows each show once: a part-watched episode replaces that show's next-up card
The episode playing right now is hidden from Up Next until playback stops, and Now Playing cards show the episode title next to the episode number
The Now Playing card no longer stays on screen after playback ends
Movies and TV cards show the title's summary; on TV the show summary replaces the episode line
App Used labels on Movies and TV cards match the dashboard and stay neutral in the Modern style
Posters-only mode on Movies and TV has rounded poster corners, and Discover cards and posters match the Movies and TV sizes
Dashboard Watch now links no longer use provider-coloured text
Watchlist, Ratings, Custom lists and Discover show Released and the release date with a gap and no dash
History no longer shows the sync status, and its size slider is removed; its posters and cards use the Movies and TV sizes
The poster, card and compact view icons have been redesigned
On narrow tablet-width screens, dashboard cards keep a fixed-width poster beside the text, and the two featured Up Next cards sit side by side
On phones, dashboard card text fits the card width and Watch Now links wrap onto a second line; Movies and TV overview cards fit the screen
Movies overview cards with long titles no longer push their details past the card edge
In Modern light, list mode column headers on History, Movies and TV Shows are easier to read
The TV Shows page keeps existing cards on screen while loading more or re-sorting by Next Airing, and refreshes its cached pages after 30 minutes so next-airing dates stay current
Modern dashboard card artwork loads as cards scroll near the screen instead of all at once

Custom Lists are now Playlists, listed above Ratings, and can be synced two ways to Plex, Emby, and Jellyfin, with the apps chosen per playlist, a Recently deleted pop-up with Delete all permanently, drag and drop reordering, and moves made in an app read back
Playlists can be Movies, TV, or Mixed; TV playlists hold separate episodes chosen with an episode picker, and neighbouring episodes of a show stack into one poster with Posters only on
Import playlists made in Plex, Emby, or Jellyfin from an Import from apps dialog, showing item counts, a type guess, and name clash hints, merged into a same-name playlist or kept separate
A playlist shows a note when an app holds items Plembfin could not identify, which stay in that app untouched, and the Missing badge sits in the top-left corner of every playlist poster

Automatic playlists fill themselves from a rule: a Type (Top rated by default, Popular, Trending this week, New releases), genres, original language (English ticked on new ones), years, watched state, and recently added, from your libraries or the TMDB catalogue, checked hourly or on Refresh now and sent one way to the apps
Automatic playlists can be ordered by rank or by full release date, default to a maximum of 20 titles, and leave out talk and news shows and library titles not yet matched to TMDB, IMDb, or TVDB

Automatic TV playlists hold the next episode to watch of each show; with the new Remove items once watched setting, watched movies and episodes leave the playlist, and with it off a watched show moves on to its next episode at the next sync

The playlist dialog is larger and wider, with its steps down the side, Settings-style choices, and a visible close button in the light theme; a new automatic playlist shows Checking the rule until its titles arrive

The Playlists page heading is tidied into TV Shows, app icon badges, an Auto tag, and one Options menu with an Info pop-up and a refresh spinner, and the page updates itself when a scheduled sync changes a playlist
Playlist posters open across the screen on phones without being cut off, and dragging on desktop shows the other cards sliding aside with a centred Move pill
Fixed Plex ignoring some playlist moves by re-reading and rebuilding its order
Modern card backdrops show on History, Discover, Watchlist, Ratings, and Playlists, and failed backdrop lookups are retried

With Posters only on, clicking a poster opens its card in place on Library, Discover, History, Watchlist, Ratings, and Playlists, and History and playlist episode posters show the episode code and name over them
Discover and Playlists poster views stay as sideways rows with posters sized to their row
Opening a Dashboard TV stack folds any other open run back into its stack
Up Next rebuilds are about twice as fast and stop re-asking every provider for titles and series they already checked
The dashboard history preview is much smaller (about 130 KB instead of 324 KB), so the dashboard loads faster
The Manual Watch review notice stays in the sidebar when a new item is flagged after an earlier review was decided
Fixed connecting Trakt, Plex, or Jellyfin getting stuck on Waiting for confirmation with Same-origin request required when Plembfin is opened by a plain HTTP LAN address

The nightly Plembfin backup is written to disk in small pieces instead of being built in memory, which needed about 3 GB for a 490 MB backup and got the server killed; a failed day is retried at most three times an hour apart, and half-written backup files from a killed run are deleted

Backblaze backups are sent from disk in small pieces, and an upload taking longer than 60 seconds is no longer cut off while it is still moving; the Backblaze setup guide links to the Backblaze pages it mentions
Backups made by the server can be restored from the Restore page, which always said the passphrase was wrong

Full Plembfin backups of any size restore on the server from the list or from an uploaded file, with upload, check, and import progress; the file is checked in full before anything changes, and large backups can be downloaded from the backup list
Opening a show's seasons for the first time is much faster (about 7 seconds down to a few milliseconds on a large library).
Movies and TV Shows grids look up posters that fail to load together in one request instead of one at a time.
The dashboard no longer asks for Up Next twice when it first loads.
The Settings page no longer makes status requests before you sign in.
Checking whether you are signed in no longer blocks the server for about 45 ms on every call.
Episode sync can now find items in Jellyfin-compatible libraries whose generic item query omits episodes.
In the Modern style, a folded TV episode stack on the dashboard no longer shows its details spilling past the card.

A scheduled step that runs past its time slot, such as a large nightly backup, is now logged as still running and then as finished, instead of a false "failed ... timed out" error; a real failure after that point is logged too.
messageFragments: Feature - Add the Modern style, fold watched runs into stacks, and show one Up Next card per show
Feature - Sync playlists with Plex, Emby, and Jellyfin, add automatic playlists, and fix large backups and restores
Performance - Faster seasons and sign-in checks, Jellyfin episode fallback, backup log and dashboard fixes
